subject: general
question: If carbon will form C⁴⁻, then the number of electrons and protons in the carbon ion will be ___________ and ___________ respectively.
solution:
The correct answer is __**10; 6**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• If carbon forms a **C4- ion**, it gains **4 additional electrons** to its neutral state.
 
• Neutral carbon has **6 protons** and **6 electrons**.
 
• Therefore, a C4- ion will have **10 electrons** (6 + 4) and **6 protons**.
 
• Hence, the number of electrons and protons in the carbon ion will be **10 and 6 respectively**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A neutral carbon atom has an atomic number of **6**, which means it has **6 protons**.
 
• In its ionized state as C4-, carbon has gained **4 extra electrons**, leading to a total of **10 electrons**.
 
• Protons remain unchanged during ionization, thus the number of protons in C4- is still **6**.
 
• This ionization process impacts the electrical charge balance but not the number of protons in the nucleus.
